purpose: Problem-family assimilation routines for M2D-SBA-05 after concept teaching and before Revised Core (2) transfer.

transfer_routines.title: Height reveals vertical launch component and flight time
recognition_signals: time of flight T is asked

method_steps.title: Check the model
method_steps.learner_move: Confirm launch and landing are at the same height.

method_steps.title: Use the apex event
method_steps.learner_move: At maximum height v_y=0, so use H=u_y^2/(2g).

method_steps.title: Recover the vertical component
method_steps.learner_move: Write u_y=sqrt(2gH).

method_steps.title: Turn vertical component into total time
method_steps.learner_move: Use T=2u_y/g and check the units.

independent_practice.prompt: A same-height projectile reaches a maximum height of 20 m. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find its initial vertical component and total time of flight.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: At the apex the vertical velocity is zero.

readiness_checks: recognise an H-to-time question
state the same-height condition first
recover u_y from H without looking
finish a fresh H-to-T problem without H2/H3
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q02 and Q22 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.

transfer_routines.title: Maximum range and the 45-degree component pattern
recognition_signals: horizontal component at maximum range may be asked

method_steps.title: Recognise the maximum-range condition
method_steps.learner_move: For same-height ideal flight, maximum range occurs at theta=45 degrees.

method_steps.title: Use the compact maximum-range relation
method_steps.learner_move: Write R_max=u^2/g.

method_steps.title: Recover the launch speed if needed
method_steps.learner_move: Use u=sqrt(gR_max).

method_steps.title: Resolve the 45-degree components
method_steps.learner_move: At 45 degrees, u_x=u_y=u/sqrt(2).

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile has maximum same-height range 80 m. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find the launch speed and its horizontal component for the maximum-range launch.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Maximum same-height range occurs at 45 degrees.

readiness_checks: identify the 45-degree condition
write R_max=u^2/g
recover u then a component
finish a fresh maximum-range problem independently
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q06 and Q12 after 4/4 readiness.

transfer_routines.title: Equal flight time and angle convention
recognition_signals: two projectiles have equal time of flight
angles may be measured from different reference directions

method_steps.title: Translate every angle to the same convention
method_steps.learner_move: Convert angles measured from vertical into angles from horizontal before resolving components.

method_steps.title: Use what equal time really means
method_steps.learner_move: For same-height flight T=2u_y/g, so equal T means equal u_y.

method_steps.title: Write each vertical component carefully
method_steps.learner_move: Use sine or cosine according to the converted angle.

method_steps.title: Equate and solve
method_steps.learner_move: Set the two vertical components equal and check the angle interpretation.

independent_practice.prompt: Projectile A is launched at speed 20 m/s at 30 degrees above horizontal. Projectile B is launched at speed V at 30 degrees from vertical. Both have the same total time of flight. Find V.
independent_practice.answer_check: B is 60 degrees above horizontal; 20 sin30 = V sin60, so V=20/sqrt(3) m/s.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Equal same-height flight time means equal initial vertical components.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Convert B's 30 degrees from vertical into 60 degrees from horizontal.

readiness_checks: spot an angle-from-vertical trap
translate angle conventions correctly
state equal T means equal u_y
solve a fresh equal-time comparison without H2/H3

transfer_routines.title: Complementary angles: equal range, different time and height

method_steps.title: Start from the range factor
method_steps.learner_move: For fixed u and g, R is proportional to sin(2theta).

method_steps.title: Recognise the complementary pair
method_steps.learner_move: Equal range for two different angles gives theta_1+theta_2=90 degrees.

method_steps.title: Do not overclaim symmetry
method_steps.learner_move: Range matches, but time and height generally do not.

method_steps.title: If heights are given, use the pair
method_steps.learner_move: Write H_1=K sin^2(theta), H_2=K cos^2(theta), so H_1+H_2=K.

independent_practice.prompt: Two same-height projectiles are launched with the same speed at complementary angles. Their maximum heights are 5 m and 15 m. Find the smaller launch angle.
independent_practice.answer_check: K=20; sin^2(theta)=5/20=1/4, so the smaller angle is 30 degrees.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Complementary shots at the same speed have equal range, but their heights use sin^2 and cos^2.

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Add the heights to get K=H_1+H_2.

readiness_checks: recognise complementary equal-range shots
state what is equal and what is not
use H_1+H_2=K
solve a fresh paired-height problem
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q16 and Q20 after 4/4 readiness.

transfer_routines.title: Compare flight time and height by ratios
recognition_signals: same launch speed for two angles
ratio of times or heights is asked

method_steps.title: Identify what stays fixed
method_steps.learner_move: Confirm u and g are common to both flights.

method_steps.title: Use the shortest proportional form
method_steps.learner_move: For time use T proportional to sin(theta); for height use H proportional to sin^2(theta).

method_steps.title: Cancel common factors
method_steps.learner_move: Compare only the angle factors.

method_steps.title: Check whether squaring is required
method_steps.learner_move: Time uses sin; height uses sin^2.

independent_practice.prompt: At the same launch speed, compare the total flight times and maximum heights for launches at 30 degrees and 60 degrees.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Common u and g cancel in a ratio.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Use T proportional to sin(theta) and H proportional to sin^2(theta).

readiness_checks: identify ratio problems before calculating full values
choose sin versus sin^2 correctly
cancel common factors cleanly
finish a fresh ratio problem without H2/H3
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q18, Q19 and Q52 after 4/4 readiness.

transfer_routines.title: Range-height ratio shortcut
recognition_signals: range R and maximum height H appear together
u or g may be unknown

method_steps.title: Check same-height validity
method_steps.learner_move: Use the shortcut only for the same-height ideal model.

method_steps.title: Write the direct ratio
method_steps.learner_move: Use R/H=4 cot(theta), or derive it if forgotten.

method_steps.title: Insert the given ratio before numbers
method_steps.learner_move: Avoid solving R and H separately.

method_steps.title: Solve the trigonometric relation and check
method_steps.learner_move: Use the size of R/H to judge whether the launch should be shallow or steep.

independent_practice.prompt: For a same-height projectile, R=4sqrt(3) H. Find the launch angle.
independent_practice.answer_check: R/H=4sqrt(3)=4cot(theta), so cot(theta)=sqrt(3) and theta=30 degrees.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: This is a direct comparison of range and maximum height in a same-height flight.

readiness_checks: recognise when the ratio shortcut is appropriate
state its validity condition
derive or recall R/H=4cot(theta)
solve a fresh ratio problem independently
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q24 and Q44 after 4/4 readiness.

transfer_routines.title: Change the launch angle to scale the range
recognition_signals: range changes by a stated factor

method_steps.title: Strip away the fixed factors
method_steps.learner_move: At fixed u and g, use R proportional to sin(2theta).

method_steps.title: Write a ratio of ranges
method_steps.learner_move: Set R_2/R_1=sin(2theta_2)/sin(2theta_1).

method_steps.title: Solve for the new sine value
method_steps.learner_move: Check it does not exceed 1.

method_steps.title: Find the possible angle pair
method_steps.learner_move: Remember sine can give two supplementary double-angles, producing complementary launch angles.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile is launched at 30 degrees. The speed is unchanged. What launch angle(s) give the same range?

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: At fixed speed, range depends only on sin(2theta).

readiness_checks: recognise fixed-speed range scaling
write the range ratio using sin(2theta)
check the required sine value is physical
find all valid launch angles

transfer_routines.title: Finish the apex/minimum-speed questions begun in SBA-04
recognition_signals: apex or minimum speed first reveals the launch angle/components
the question then asks for range or a range-height quantity

method_steps.title: Reuse the SBA-04 result
method_steps.learner_move: At apex v_min=u cos(theta); use the speed information to recover theta or the component ratio.

method_steps.title: Choose the new same-height relation
method_steps.learner_move: Use R, H or R/H according to what the question asks.

method_steps.title: Substitute only after the angle/component relation is known
method_steps.learner_move: Keep the two reasoning stages separate.

method_steps.title: Check both model conditions
method_steps.learner_move: Confirm the apex event and same-height-flight assumptions are both satisfied.

independent_practice.prompt: A same-height projectile has minimum speed equal to 0.8 times its launch speed. Find R/H.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Minimum speed occurs at the apex and equals u cos(theta).

readiness_checks: separate the SBA-04 apex step from the SBA-05 same-height step
recover angle/component ratio from minimum speed
select R/H or another same-height relation appropriately
finish a cross-bucket problem without H2/H3
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q14 and Q27 only after both SBA-04 and SBA-05 readiness are satisfied.
